PullRequest.Title: editor: ignore stale multi-diff document resolutions
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #307899 (the stale-refresh corruption path described below).

## Summary

- Invalidate an asynchronous multi-diff document batch when its observable evaluation is replaced or disposed.
- Prevent an older SCM resource snapshot from publishing references that have already been released.
- Add deterministic regression tests for resource replacement, removal, and editor input disposal.

## Reproduction and scope

The original issue reports repeated file headers. Ordinary scrolling, collapse/expand, and Git refresh did **not** reproduce that literal symptom on current main.

A delayed SCM document provider did reproduce a related corruption path in Code OSS:

1. Open a multi-diff containing an existing resource.
2. Start a resource refresh containing that resource and a slow-resolving document.
3. Replace the resource list before the slow document finishes.
4. Let the obsolete refresh finish.

Before this fix, the obsolete batch republishes the removed resource, attempts to attach its disposed text models, reports `Model is disposed!`, and blanks the multi-diff. The same scenario passes with this fix. This PR targets that reproducible race; it does not claim that every historical repeated-header cause was reproduced.

## Validation

- The new replacement regression failed on the baseline: the published sequence incorrectly returned to `removed.ts` after `current.ts`, with a disposed-model error.
- All **21 targeted tests** pass across multi-diff input, SCM resolution, widget behavior, and template virtualization, including the three new regression cases.
- `npm run compile-client` completed with zero compilation errors; the remaining built-in Copilot extension was also built.
- Targeted ESLint and `git diff --check` pass.
- **11 Code OSS UI scenario steps pass** on Windows x64, Code OSS **1.140.0 Dev**:
  - Delayed document resolution, replacing the SCM resource list, completing the obsolete refresh, and scrolling the surviving diffs.
  - Built-in Git Open Changes, repeated scrolling, collapse/expand, staging/unstaging, keyboard change navigation and collapse, inline/side-by-side layouts, and closing/reopening the editor.
- Independent **GPT-6 Astra / max** and **Claude Opus 5.5 / max** reviews: no findings.

The large collapse/expand stress run also emits development listener-count warnings. The baseline and fixed builds emitted the same eight warnings with the same listener counts; those pre-existing warnings are outside this patch's scope.

## Baseline reproduction recording (before the fix)

Recorded in Windows x64 Code OSS 1.140.0 Dev at baseline `d912aa0ec55e578a95a65b39e7fd112d317dfdc6`, before the production fix. A test SCM provider deliberately holds one document resolution while newer changes replace the resource list. Releasing the obsolete refresh causes a `Model is disposed!` error and blanks the multi-diff; the failed final validation is expected in this before-fix recording.

This demonstrates the stale-refresh race addressed by this PR, **not the historical repeated-header symptom**. It is the original baseline recording, not a result from the ongoing independent investigation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an SCM, chat/session, notebook, or explicit-resource multi-diff editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Source resolution must complete, then every current document pair's model-reference promises are awaited by Promise.all before the initial document list and downstream diff view models can publish. The added cancellation-token allocation and final boolean check are synchronous constant work; they add no awaited operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve cold file-backed text models through ITextFileService.files.resolve; remote file schemes can transit through their registered provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one underlying cold resolution per distinct canonical file URI; up to 2N acquisitions are coalesced for duplicate/live URIs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same model-reference calls, cardinality, concurrent launch, and all-items barrier existed before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All current-item model promises must settle before the initial multi-diff document list publishes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve cold virtual-document content through registered ITextModelContentProvider implementations, which may be extension-host backed depending on URI scheme.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one coalesced cold provider resolution per distinct canonical virtual URI while its reference is live or in flight.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Virtual-content resolution was already performed by createModelReference before the changed lifecycle guard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A slow current virtual document delays the all-items publication barrier.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N diff items, with at most 2N model-reference acquisitions and one cold underlying load per distinct canonical URI after global reference coalescing; duplicate URIs and already-live models do not create additional underlying loads.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All distinct cold original/modified model loads are launched concurrently by the pre-existing Promise.allSettled calls, and the batch Promise.all waits for all items. There is no limiter, but the diff neither increases this concurrency nor schedules another batch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: mapObservableArrayCached reuses promises for stable original/modified URI-pair keys. TextModelResolverService canonicalizes URIs and ReferenceCollection coalesces live and in-flight loads process-wide. Failed acquisitions release their reference and can be retried; the new token does not change positive, negative, or warm-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the production diff adds only cancelOnDispose(reader.store) and an isCancellationRequested check after the existing Promise.all.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Real N, provider latency, and the proportion of remote/virtual URIs vary by source, but the unchanged call path and cardinality are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. One small source/token/disposable allocation per active batch is bounded and replaces on recomputation; no boundary, fan-out, serialization, or critical-path wait was added.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh or replace a live multi-diff resource list while one or more model resolutions are slow
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The newest resource generation still waits for its own current model promises before publishing. Superseded generations may finish in the background, but the new cancellation check prevents them from republishing stale document objects and triggering obsolete downstream diff/render work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve models for newly introduced file-backed original/modified URIs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to two acquisitions per newly keyed pair, with one cold underlying file/provider load per distinct canonical URI after coalescing; stable keys perform no new acquisition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same acquisitions and overlapping generations ran before the PR, but an obsolete completed generation could publish after replacement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only loads belonging to the newest generation gate the desired publication; obsolete loads can complete off that generation's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve newly introduced extension-backed virtual documents when their URI content provider is remote to the workbench.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced cold provider request per distinct new canonical virtual URI, subject to provider implementation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provider requests were already launched and not cancellable here; the PR does not add or repeat them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Current-generation requests delay current publication; superseded requests continue but their result is no longer propagated downstream by the changed guard.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A changed generation with A newly keyed resource pairs causes up to 2A model acquisitions; stable pair keys reuse cached promises. Multiple rapid generations can have overlapping pre-existing loads for distinct added keys.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cold loads for newly keyed URIs run concurrently, and generations can overlap because the guard does not cancel I/O. This concurrency was pre-existing; the change only marks an old derived evaluation when its store is disposed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Stable URI-pair promises remain cached by mapObservableArrayCached. Removed-key stores release references; if a load completes after removal, the item callback detects its disposed store and releases the resulting references. Global canonical-URI reference coalescing still applies. The cancellation token itself is disposed/replaced with each derived evaluation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: derived recomputation disposes the previous reader store, cancelOnDispose flips that generation's token, and the added check executes before documents.set.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Refresh burst size and provider duration vary, especially for SCM and chat-driven sources. The maximum avoided stale downstream work depends on how many obsolete documents resolve after replacement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; the change reduces obsolete downstream CPU/rendering and disposed-object retention without increasing boundary cardinality or concurrency. It does not optimize pre-existing uncancelled model loads, but that is not introduced by this diff.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close or dispose a multi-diff editor while document models are still resolving
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After disposal there is no user-visible progress path to gate. Existing in-flight resolutions may complete, their per-item disposed stores release references, and the new disposed derived store marks the batch so it cannot publish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Completion of file-backed model resolutions already started before editor disposal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded by the pending distinct cold URIs at disposal; disposal starts zero additional operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same in-flight operations completed after close; before the PR their batch continuation could still attempt publication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the user-visible critical path after close, though resources remain occupied until the underlying non-cancellable resolution settles.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Completion of already-started virtual-document provider requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded by pending distinct cold virtual URIs at disposal, with reference coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The PR neither starts nor cancels these requests; it only suppresses their obsolete aggregate publication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the closed editor's critical path; completion is needed only for cleanup of the acquired reference.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Up to two already-started model acquisitions per pending resource pair at close time; no new acquisitions are started by disposal or by the added guard.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The already-running pre-existing acquisitions continue at their original concurrency because ITextModelService.createModelReference has no cancellation token on this path. The new token controls only post-await publication.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-item stores release completed references for removed/disposed entries; ReferenceCollection drops the canonical URI entry at zero references and disposes the resolved model according to text-file lifecycle rules. The guard token and its disposable are themselves released with the derived store.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: model acquisition precedes the changed lines, while the added token observes disposal and skips only documents.set.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number and duration of requests still pending at close depend on source size and provider speed, but no changed mechanism increases them.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable cleanup or memory regression. The changed lifecycle check prevents stale publication, and all newly allocated cancellation state is bounded to the derived evaluation.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff and traced initial open, live replacement/removal, and disposal through model resolution, caches, concurrency, cleanup, and downstream publication. No actionable performance regression was introduced. The PR's demonstrated symptom is correctness corruption/blanking rather than a measured or strongly evidenced shipped performance symptom, so no regression-fix learning record was submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
